correctness.rationale: In the synchronous product on Q×Q, advance along any pair S⊆T; a reachable state in F×(Q\F) is precisely a failure, since only equal-length words are compared. Reachability in this implicit product is in NL: store two states and a counter bounded by |Q|², and scan the explicit table for successors. NL=coNL gives membership also for monotonicity. DFA nonemptiness with a nonaccepting start is NL-hard by reachability from a fresh start: use edge choices as transition labels, other moves to a sink, and the target as final. Complementation gives source emptiness NL-completeness. In the stated reduction every valid block has length m>=2 and precisely one occurring predicate. The parser needs only the simulated state, the position in the block, and the seen predicate position (or none), so its explicit transitions are streamed in logspace and there are O(|Q|m²) states. A nonempty accepted source word has a coded block in which flipping one bottom letter to top makes a rejected block; the empty source language maps to the empty language. The nonaccepting start is essential to this proof because the empty word has no upward perturbation. Larger fixed powerset alphabets can reject unused letters; k=0 gives equality of all equal-length words. No finite sampling was needed.

On the binary chain 0<1, for every reachable q the right language at δ(q,0) must be included in that at δ(q,1). Necessity follows from prefixing a word reaching q; sufficiency follows by changing one coordinate at a time.

value.rationale: One predicate is the smallest nontrivial ordered vocabulary. Resolving it distinguishes hardness due to the state reachability structure from hardness due to a growing alphabet and makes the dichotomy with zero predicates exact. This is a meaningful restriction of the complexity theorem, not a repetition of the known product upper bound.
